body: I also encountered the same bug, have you solved it now?
Unfortunately not, I haven't been able to investigate further.

I _think_ I may have found the (or at least _a_) cause (and have a potential resolution) to this issue.

The short answer is that its a race condition between the .NET Finalizer thread and the main thread. When you create a C# object, it grabs or creates a reference to a `CSharpScript` object (the Godot `Resource` representation of each .NET `Type`). These scripts, once constructed, are held in a global cache dictionary lookup table thing, and (importantly and infuriatingly) are _removed_ from it when destructed.

At some point, what is happening is there is an object in your game where it is the only instance of that class (and thus the only ref to that `CSharpScript`) alive at that exact moment, then it gets garbage collected leading to a cascade where its corresponding `CSharpScript` gets destroyed as well. While it (the `CSharpScript`), is being destroyed, but before its reached the point where it has a chance to remove itself from the global cache table, _another_ part of your code is trying to _initialize_ another instance of that same class, and so is trying to grab the (now invalid) reference to that `CSharpScript` object from the cache. The system is intelligent enough to return a `null` ref from the table when it noticed the object is pending deletion, but it _doesn't_ treat it as missing, and so the code happily goes on trying to initialize a new object with a `null` class ref.

I was able to write a fairly simple (though maybe a bit hack) fix to a custom build of the engine, where _if_ the main thread tries to pull a `CSharpScript` from the cache that it identifies is invalid, it will pre-emptively remove it from the table right away, and proceed as if it was not found. This seems to work correctly: when the Finalizer thread subsequently gets to removing the ref from the table, it will just silently find that it has already been removed and move on with its life. I'll try to post a branch and a PR (though lord knows when or if it would be accepted), but if you want a quick fix in the meantime: Just create a global `List<CSharpScript>` of all the scripts in your game so that those resources never get GC'd.

Though I think this elides the bigger question, which is why is Godot so aggressive about removing script references from its cache?
